When a web link is shared in a busy team channel, a useful roundup often includes more than the page title. The best summaries briefly identify what each page says, why it was shared, and any relevant surrounding discussion that helps readers understand the link later.

For internal QA of roundup quality, some teams maintain a temporary context ledger: a single plain-text record containing the available channel excerpts in chronological order.   2. Open each linked page and write a short neutral description of its contents.
  3. Review the broader workspace discussion only as background context.
